## User story

**As an** operator,
**I want** to check the API and each cloud dependency independently,
**so that** I can distinguish a running process from a service that is ready to analyze and save scans.

## Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — Independent readiness**
Given Gemini, Firestore, Pub/Sub and BigQuery are available,
when I request `GET /api/health`,
then HTTP 200 reports each dependency's readiness independently, plus the configured project and region, normally `asia-southeast1`.

**AC2 — Degraded is not a crashed probe**
Given any one dependency is unavailable,
when I request health,
then HTTP 200 reports a degraded state and identifies that dependency without falsely marking the others unavailable.

**AC3 — Bounded checks**
Given one readiness check stalls,
when I request health,
then it reports that dependency as unavailable within the agreed per-check and overall timeout budgets, both `TBD (OQ-5)`.

**AC4 — Safe health output**
Given dependency checks succeed or fail,
when health is returned,
then the response contains no credentials, tokens, raw cloud payloads or full client configuration.

## Tasks

- [x] Expose an async `GET /api/health` route
- [x] Include environment-selected project ID in the current response
- [ ] Add independent readiness results and configured region
- [ ] Use bounded, non-blocking checks through the existing service boundaries
- [ ] Return HTTP 200 with degraded details instead of throwing when a dependency is down
- [ ] Agree numeric readiness budgets under OQ-5 and add safe-output/timeout tests

## Current state

The route always returns `status=operational` and the project ID. It performs no readiness checks and omits the region. The backlog remains blocked on analysis, telemetry, storage and publisher prerequisites and OQ-5.

| Gap                                          | Impact                                                                                |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Unconditional operational status             | The probe can claim readiness while analysis, persistence or telemetry is unavailable |
| No independent dependency statuses or region | Operators cannot localize failures or verify the configured region                    |
| No timeout policy                            | Numeric degraded-response acceptance cannot be frozen before OQ-5 is answered         |

Readiness orchestration follows the [FastAPI instructions](../../instructions/fastapi-backend.instructions.md); synchronous checks must not block the event loop. No new arbitrary timeout value is introduced here.

## Test cases

| Test                                                      | Asserts                                                                                |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `test_health_reports_all_dependencies_project_and_region` | Healthy response includes four independent readiness results and configuration         |
| `test_health_dependency_failure_returns_200_degraded`     | One failed dependency does not collapse the whole probe                                |
| `test_health_stalled_dependency_respects_agreed_timeout`  | Stalling produces degraded output within OQ-5 budgets; blocked until values are agreed |
| `test_health_output_excludes_secrets_and_raw_errors`      | Both healthy and degraded responses are safe                                           |

## Definition of done

OQ-5 timeout budgets are agreed, all four cases pass with mocked dependencies, HTTP 200 remains stable during degradation, and coverage stays at least 70%. No live cloud calls enter automated QA.
